name: Marsannay

limits: For white wine, Pinot Gris: at most 10%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for rosé, 57 for white, 50 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.

blurb.text: A Côte de Nuits appellation, the only village appellation in Burgundy allowed to make rosé. Red wine from Pinot Noir is about 70 percent of production, rosé comes from Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris, and white from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc. It has no Grand Cru or Premier Cru vineyards.
